prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Edit the supplied single starting illustration into ONE3-by-3 sheet of NINE SQUARE equal panels, tightly tiled without gutters or labels. Preserve exactly the same muscular man, body proportions, natural skin colour/texture, graphite machine, black shorts/shoes, lighting, background and front-three-quarter camera of the input. Full scene at identical scale in every cell. FIRST panel is the actual input starting pose, not a redesigned apparatus. These are nine progressive positions of ONE seated abdominal crunch, in row-major order:0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32degrees of controlled upper torso flexion. Every one of the9 cells must be different gradual progress, not repeated start panels and a jump at the end.
ARCHITECTURE MUST REMAIN THE INPUT: single overhead work-arm yoke turning about a TRANSVERSE HORIZONTAL axis behind the shoulders, two high rubber grips held beside the neck/upper shoulders. This is an abdominal crunch machine, not a pec-deck: no two vertical swivels above the head and no new butterfly arms. The fixed work-arm bearing, cable pulleys, enclosed tower, floor chassis, footrests, seat pedestal and lumbar pad stay at the same coordinates in every panel. The work arm pivots forward/down as a rigid bent tube with constant shape and thickness, no changing topology or telescoping. Keep its rounded contour clear of the man's head and preserve natural depth occlusion.
MOTION: pelvis remains anchored in the seat, thighs/knees/shins/feet exactly fixed and both shoes fully supported. CURL ribs toward pelvis by flexing the trunk with visible, modest spinal rounding; shoulders/head progressively travel forward/down away from the fixed back support. Do not simply nod the neck or hinge the whole straight torso at the hips. The neck follows the curve of the upper torso naturally. BOTH hands stay firmly around the same two high grips beside the neck/shoulders throughout, with bent elbows; the arms remain close to the body and do not do an arm pulldown. Hands and high yoke travel together. Mild natural elbow-angle adaptation follows the fixed-length work arm, but the hands remain close to the neck and no body segment stretches. At the last pose, upper back is visibly curled and abdomen shortened, face/chin angled with the torso, hips and legs unchanged. Fixed seat and lumbar pad must not follow the torso. No backrest sticking to the moving body, no steel passing through face/neck/arms, no weight plates multiplying, no logos, text, arrows or numbers. Realistic coloured instructional render, not video-game character.
